_comment: GOLDEN-REGENERATION INTEGRITY GATE — provenance allowlist (issue #122).
Goldens/vectors are self-produced by the implementation-under-test. This file
is how a PR carries an INDEPENDENT justification for changing one. Every entry
pins a specific golden file to the exact NEW content it is authorizing, via a
sha256 of that file's bytes. Because the pin is content-addressed, an entry can
only ever justify the ONE value it was reviewed for — a later, different
regeneration of the same file fails the gate again and forces a fresh entry.
See conformance/README.md -> 'Golden-regeneration integrity gate' for the full
design and the two ways to satisfy the gate.
Schema of each entry in `entries`:
path             (string, required)  repo-root-relative path of the golden file
sha256           (string, required)  hex sha256 of the file's NEW (post-change) bytes
verified-against (enum,   required)  one of: official-KAT | second-implementation |
differential-oracle | intentional-spec-change
reason           (string, required)  human explanation of WHY the new bytes are correct
and against WHICH independent oracle they were checked
reviewer         (string, required)  who signed the entry off. A real reviewer is a GitHub
handle ('gh:alice'). An entry produced by a tool or an agent
and NOT yet reviewed by a human MUST say so: use
'unreviewed:<producer>' and set review-status below. The gate
only checks that the field is non-empty, so a fabricated
handle would pass it — the honesty of this field is the whole
point of the record, and pre-filling one by convention makes
the record worse than having none.
review-status    (enum,   optional)  'unreviewed' while no human has checked the entry; omit (or
'reviewed') once one has. Entries added before this field
existed do not carry it.
date             (string, optional)  ISO date the entry was added
To compute the sha256 of a golden after you have regenerated it:
shasum -a 256 conformance/tests/<fixture>/expected-script.hex
or run the checker with --print-hashes to get them for the whole changed set.

RFC 6979 Appendix A.2.5 (P-256) + A.2.6 (P-384) deterministic-ECDSA test vectors, With-SHA-256 variant (matches the native verify path). Independently published, not compiler-produced.

Regenerated for deep-review finding C27 (else-present N-field stack reconcile). spend()'s len(scratch)-driven if/else writes BOTH state fields (count:bigint + tag:ByteString) on each arm; the pre-fix 05-stack-lower N-result reconcile was gated on empty-else, so this else-present multi-field write fell through to a single stackMap name for N results and emitted an unspendable OP_NUM2BIN continuation (silently uniform across all 7 tiers — parity-green-but-wrong). The fix broadens the reconcile to the else-present path, growing the script +5 bytes (1081->1086). Verified against the differential-execution oracle: conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/branched-readonly-len.json drives deploy->call->@bsv/sdk Spend for BOTH branches (count 5->6/tag->4142 and count 5->4/tag->3030) plus a tampered-output reject — all validate. Also corroborated by 7-tier cross-compiler byte-identical parity (fold-off and fold-on).

New fixture for deep-review finding C20 (dropped terminal assert(false) else). set()'s if(i==0)/elif(i==1)/else{assert(false)} dispatch is exactly the shape whose abort the pre-fix 04-anf-lower liftBranchUpdateProps silently dropped, letting an out-of-range selector produce a spendable no-op state continuation. No existing conformance fixture exercised this shape, so C20 had zero cross-tier codegen coverage; this fixture is that gate. The compiled script encodes the re-emitted assert(cond0 || cond1). Verified against the differential-execution oracle: conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/selector.json drives set(0,99)/set(1,99) accept plus the out-of-range set(2,99) reject through @bsv/sdk Spend (the abort fires on-chain). Corroborated by 7-tier cross-compiler byte-identical parity (fold-off and fold-on) across all 9 input formats.

ecAdd could not DOUBLE a point: the affine chord slope (qy-py)/(qx-px) divides by zero when P==Q, so ecAdd(P,P) produced a wrong point and any contract that doubled deployed an UNSPENDABLE script — byte-identically across all seven tiers. affineAdd now selects the tangent numerator and denominator before the single fieldInv. These bytes are the regenerated output of that fix. INDEPENDENT ORACLE: the emitted script is executed against the real @bsv/sdk interpreter in packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/ec-add-doubling.test.ts and checked against the known secp256k1 group elements — ecAdd(G,2G)==3G (chord path unchanged), ecAdd(G,G)==2G and ecAdd(2G,2G)==4G (doubling fixed), with ecMulGen(3)==3G as a control. The original defect was first observed as a real regtest-node rejection of the ec-unit fixture. Cross-tier: conformance 65/65 with no tier-vs-tier divergence; Zig and Go verified byte-identical on the same ecAdd ANF.

Re-stamped after the ecAdd doubling fix. Only the five EC fixtures moved, by +0.05%..+0.09% (convergence-proof, ec-demo, ec-primitives, ec-unit, schnorr-zkp) — the tangent-slope selection adds 124 ops and reuses the single existing fieldInv. All 60 other fixtures are byte-unchanged.

Codegen change, +42 bytes: ecMul / ecMulGen now reduce the scalar to [0, n-1] before the k+3n ladder offset (+42 bytes per call), so k >= n, k < 0 and k = 0 are defined instead of silently yielding a different multiple of P.
